novelty_flags.label: Proposition strong-fwer
novelty_flags.one_line: Arithmetic e-merging plus closure already supplies strong FWER; the proposed proposition is a direct Gaussian sequential specialization, not an independent novelty result.

novelty_flags.label: Theorem simultaneous-lower-sequences
novelty_flags.one_line: The displayed scalar e-process inversion, coordinatewise time-uniform validity, and union-bound calibration are standard confidence-sequence machinery.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper states a general continuous-time Gaussian-diffusion and allocation-process representation for adaptive experiments, with applications including regret and e-processes.

Under weak signals of order n^{-1/2}, sequential experiments with state-continuous allocation probabilities converge weakly to an SDE diffusion; the source also identifies Lipschitz state dependence as a regularity condition.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv v4 corresponding to Annals of Statistics 49(3), 2021
source_verification_receipts.locator: Section 3, Theorem 3.2; Section 5, especially lines 175--247 of the HTML rendering
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Arithmetic averaging is an e-merging rule and the paper explicitly presents closure-based multiple-testing procedures with familywise validity.

source_verification_receipts.version: Statistics in Medicine 40, 2021 published open-access version
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper uses a closed testing procedure for strong FWER and optimizes enrichment for a specified prior and gain via posterior expected gain.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Theorem 2 and sparse-linear-program construction described in the article text
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The published method jointly optimizes two-stage enrichment decisions and multiple-testing procedures through a discretized sparse linear program.
The paper studies finite-horizon dynamic programming for design-optimal e-values in single-arm binary trials and names multi-arm and response-adaptive extensions as future settings.
The article develops nonasymptotic time-uniform confidence sequences from exponential-supermartingale methods, including mixture and stitching constructions.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Move strong FWER and simultaneous lower confidence sequences out of the novelty-bearing result list into explicitly cited supporting corollaries; keep the new boundary-stability, value-transfer, and certificate claims as the paper’s theorem-level kernel.

State an explicit certificate input encoding, termination/complexity bound, and dependence of mesh, truncation, quadrature, and prior-net sizes on epsilon_cert; this would make the constructive claim independently auditable.

Add a worked nontrivial K>=2 finite-scenario certificate instance that reports the computed interval, least-favorable prior, policy mixture, and each separated error contribution from primitive inputs.

recommended_next_step: Revise by demoting the two published-routine inference statements to supporting corollaries, then advance the boundary-stable frontier and certified dynamic-program kernel to Stage 0.
